\section*{AP \({ }^{\text {® }}\) CALCULUS AB \\ 2011 SCORING GUIDELINES (Form B)}

\section*{Question 1}

A cylindrical can of radius 10 millimeters is used to measure rainfall in Stormville. The can is initially empty, and rain enters the can during a 60-day period. The height of water in the can is modeled by the function \(S\), where \(S(t)\) is measured in millimeters and \(t\) is measured in days for \(0 \leq t \leq 60\). The rate at which the height of the water is rising in the can is given by \(S^{\prime}(t)=2 \sin (0.03 t)+1.5\).
\begin{itemize}
\item[(a)] According to the model, what is the height of the water in the can at the end of the 60-day period?
\item[(b)] According to the model, what is the average rate of change in the height of water in the can over the 60-day period? Show the computations that lead to your answer. Indicate units of measure.
\item[(c)] Assuming no evaporation occurs, at what rate is the volume of water in the can changing at time \(t=7\) ? Indicate units of measure.
\item[(d)] During the same 60-day period, rain on Monsoon Mountain accumulates in a can identical to the one in Stormville. The height of the water in the can on Monsoon Mountain is modeled by the function \(M\), where \(M(t)=\frac{1}{400}\left(3 t^{3}-30 t^{2}+330 t\right)\). The height \(M(t)\) is measured in millimeters, and \(t\) is measured in days for \(0 \leq t \leq 60\). Let \(D(t)=M^{\prime}(t)-S^{\prime}(t)\). Apply the Intermediate Value Theorem to the function \(D\) on the interval \(0 \leq t \leq 60\) to justify that there exists a time \(t, 0<t<60\), at which the heights of water in the two cans are changing at the same rate.
\item[(a)] \(S(60)=\int_{0}^{60} S^{\prime}(t) d t=171.813 \mathrm{~mm}\)
\item[(b)] \(\frac{S(60)-S(0)}{60}=2.863\) or \(2.864 \mathrm{~mm} /\) day
\item[(c)] \(V(t)=100 \pi S(t)\)
\(V^{\prime}(7)=100 \pi S^{\prime}(7)=602.218\)
The volume of water in the can is increasing at a rate of \(602.218 \mathrm{~mm}^{3} /\) day .
\item[(d)] \(D(0)=-0.675<0\) and \(D(60)=69.37730>0\)
Because \(D\) is continuous, the Intermediate Value Theorem implies that there is a time \(t, 0<t<60\), at which \(D(t)=0\).
At this time, the heights of water in the two cans are changing at the same rate.
\item[] \(3:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { limits } \\ 1: \text { integrand } \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[1] : answer
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1 \text { : relationship between } V \text { and } S \\ 1: \text { answer }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[] \(2:\left\{\begin{array}{l}1: \text { considers } D(0) \text { and } D(60) \\ 1: \text { justification }\end{array}\right.\)
\item[1] : units in (b) or (c)
\end{itemize}
